chapters.title_en: On the Permissibility of Prophetic Mission and the Refutation of Its Impossibility
chapters.arabic_text:
ندعي أن بعثة الأنبياء جائز، وليس بمحال ولا واجب، وقالت المعتزلة إنه
واجب، وقد سبق وجه الرد عليهم. وقالت البراهمة إنه محال، وبرهان الجواز أنه
مهما قام الدليل على أن الله تعالى متكلم وقام الدليل على أنه قادر لا يعجز
على أن يدل على كلام النفس بخلق ألفاظ وأصوات ورقوم أو غيرها من الدلالات،
وقد قام دليل على جواز إرسال الرسل، فإنا لسنا نعني به إلا أن يقوم بذات
الله تعالى خبر عن الأمر النافع في الآخرة والأمر الضار بحكم إجراء العادة،
ويصدر منه فعل هو دلالة الشخص على ذلك الخبر وعلى أمره بتبليغ الخبر، ويصدر
منه فعل خارق للعادة مقرونا
بدعوى ذلك الشخص الرسالة، فليس شيء من ذلك محالا لذاته، فإنه يرجع إلى
كلام النفس وإلى اختراع ما هو دلالة على الكلام وما هو مصدق للرسول وإن حكم
باستحالة ذلك من حيث الاستقباح والاستحسان، فقد استأصلنا هذا الأصل في  حق
الله تعالى ثم لا يمكن أن يدعي قبح إرسال الرسول على قانون الاستقباح،
فالمعتزلة مع المصير إلى ذلك لم يستقبحوا هذا فليس إدراك قبحه ولا إدراك
امتناعه في ذاته ضروريا فلا بد من ذكر سببه. وغاية ما هو به ثلاثة شبه:
الأولى: قولهم: إنه لو بعث النبي بما تقتضيه العقول ففي العقول غنية عنه
وبعثة الرسول عبث، وذلك وعلى الله محال، وإن بعث بما يخالف العقول استحال
التصديق والقبول.
الثانية: إنه يستحيل العبث لأنه يستحيل تعريف صدقه، لأن الله تعالى لو
شافه الخلق بتصديقه وكلمهم جهارا فلا حاجة إلى رسول، وإن لم يشافه به
فغايته الدلالة على صدقه بفعل خارق للعادة، ولا يتميز ذلك عن السحر
والطلسمات وعجائب الخواص وهي خارقة للعادات عند من لا يعرفها، وإذا استويا
في خرق العادة لم يؤمن ذلك فلا يحصل العلم بالتصديق.
الثالثة: إنه إن عرف تمييزها عن السحر والطلسمات والتخيلات فمن أين يعرف
الصدق؟ ولعل الله تعالى أراد إضلالنا وإغواءنا بتصديقه ولعل كل ما قال
النبي إنه مسعد فهو مشقي، وكلما قال مشقي فهو مسعد، ولكن الله أراد أن
يسوقنا إلى الهلاك ويغوينا بقول الرسول، فإن الإضلال والإغواء غير محال على
الله تعالى عندكم، إذ العقل لا يحسن ولا يقبح؛ وهذه أقوى شبهة ينبغي أن
يجادل بها المعتزلي عند رومه إلزام القول بتقبيح العقل، إذ يقول: إن لم يكن
الاغواء قبيحا فلا يعرف صدق الرسل قط ولا يعلم أنه ليس باضلال. والجواب أن
نقول:
أما الشبهة الأولى فضعيفة؛ فإن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يرد مخبرا بما
لا تشتغل العقول بمعرفته، ولكن تستقل بفهمه إذا عرف، فإن العقل لا يرشد إلى
النافع والضار من الأعمال والأقوال والأخلاق والعقائد، ولا يفرق بين المشقى
والمسعد، كما لا يستقل بدرك خواص الأدوية والعقاقير، ولكنه إذا عرف فهم
وصدق وانتفع بالسماع فيجتنب الهلاك ويقصد المسعد، كما ينتفع بقول الطبيب في
معرفة الداء والدواء، ثم كما يعرف صدق الطبيب بقرائن الأحوال وأمور أخر،
فكذلك يستدل على صدق  الرسول عليه السلام بمعجزات وقرائن وحالات فلا فرق.
فأما الشبهة الثانية، وهو عدم تمييز المعجزة عن السحر والتخيل، فليس
كذلك. فإن أحدا من العقلاء لم يجوز انتهاء السحر إلى إحياء الموتى، وقلب
العصا ثعبانا،
وفلق القمر، وشق البحر، وإبراء الأكمه والأبرص، وأمثال ذلك. والقول
الوجيز إن هذا القائل إن ادعى أن كل مقدور لله تعالى فهو ممكن تحصيله
بالسحر فهو قول معلوم الاستحالة بالضرورة، وإن فرق بين فعل قوم وفعل قوم
فقد تصور تصديق الرسول بما يعلم أنه ليس من السحر ويبقى النظر بعده في
أعيان الرسل عليهم السلام وآحاد المعجزات وأن ما أظهروه من جنس ما يمكن
تحصيله بالسحر أم لا، ومهما وقع الشك فيه لم يحصل التصديق به ما لم يتحد به
النبي على ملأ من أكابر السحرة ولم يمهلهم مدة المعارضة ولم يعجزوا عنه،
وليس الآن من غرضنا آحاد المعجزات.
وأما الشبهة الثالثة، وهو تصور الإغواء من الله تعالى والتشكيك لسبب ذلك،
فنقول: مهما علم وجه دلالة المعجزة على صدق النبي، علم أن ذلك مأمون عليه،
وذلك بأن يعرف الرسالة ومعناها ويعرف وجه الدلالة فنقول: لو تحدى إنسان بين
يدي ملك على جنده أنه رسول الملك إليهم وأن الملك أوجب طاعته عليهم في قسمة
الأرزاق والاقطاعات، فطالبوه بالبرهان والملك ساكت، فقال: أيها الملك إن
كنت صادقا في ما ادعيته فصدقني بأن تقوم على سريرك ثلاث مرات على التوالي
وتقعد على خلاف عادتك؛ فقام الملك عقيب التماسه على التوالي ثلاث مرات ثم
قعد، حصل للحاضرين على ضروري بأنه رسول الملك قبل أن يخطر ببالهم أن هذا
الملك من عادته الإغواء أم يستحيل في حقه ذلك. بل لو قال الملك صدقت وقد
جعلت رسولا ووكيلا لعلم أنه وكيل ورسول، فإذا خالف العادة بفعله كان ذلك
كقوله أنت رسولي، وهذا ابتداء نصب وتولية وتفويض، ولا يتصور الكذب في
التفويض وإنما يتصور في الإخبار، والعلم يكون هذا تصديقا وتفويضا ضروريا،
ولذلك لم ينكر أحد صدق الأنبياء من هذه الجهة، بل أنكروا  كون ما جاء به
الأنبياء خارقا للعادة وحملوه على السحر والتلبيس أو أنكروا وجود رب متكلم
آمر ناه مصدق مرسل، فأما من اعترف بجميع ذلك واعترف بكون المعجزة فعل الله
تعالى حصل له العلم الضروري بالتصديق. فإن قيل: فهب أنهم رأوا الله تعالى
بأعينهم وسمعوه بآذانهم وهو يقول هذا رسولي ليخبركم بطريق سعادتكم
وشقاوتكم، فما الذي يؤمنكم أنه أغوى الرسول والمرسل إليه وأخبر عن المشقى
بأنه مسعد وعن المسعد بأنه مشقى فإن ذلك غير محال إذا لم تقولوا بتقبيح
العقول؟ بل لو قدر عدم الرسول ولكن قال الله تعالى شفاها وعيانا ومشاهدة:
نجاتكم في الصوم والصلاة والزكاة وهلاككم في تركها، فبم نعلم صدقه؟ فلعله
يلبس علينا ليغوينا ويهلكنا، فإن الكذب عندكم ليس قبيحا لعينه وإن كان
قبيحا فلا يمتنع على الله تعالى ما هو قبيح وظلم، وما فيه فيه هلاك الخلق
أجمعين.
والجواب: إن الكذب مأمون عليه، فإنه إنما يكون في الكلام وكلام الله
تعالى ليس بصوت ولا حرف حتى يتطرق إليه التلبيس بل هو معنى قائم بنفسه
سبحانه، فكل ما يعلمه الإنسان يقوم بذاته خبر عن معلومه على وفق علمه ولا
يتصور الكذب فيه، وكذلك في حق الله تعالى. وعلى الجملة: الكذب في كلام
النفس محال وفي ذلك الأمن عما قالوه. وقد اتضح بهذا أن الفعل مهما علم أنه
فعل الله تعالى وأنه خارج عن مقدور البشر واقترن بدعوى النبوة حصل العلم
الضروري بالصدق وكان الشك من حيث الشك في أنه مقدور البشر أم لا، فأما بعد
معرفته كونه من فعل الله تعالى لا يبقى للشك مجال أصلا البتة. فإن قيل فهل
تجوزون الكرامات؟ قلنا: اختلف الناس فيه، والحق ذلك جائز فإنه يرجع إلى خرق
الله تعالى العادة بدعاء إنسان أو عند حاجته وذلك مما لا يستحيل في نفسه
لأنه ممكن، ولا يؤدي إلى محال آخر، فإنه لا يؤدي إلى بطلان المعجزة لأن
الكرامة عبارة عما يظهر من غير اقتران التحدي به، فإن كان مع التحدي فإنا
نسميه معجزة  ويدل بالضرورة على صدق المتحدي؛ وإن لم تكن دعوى فقد يجوز ظهور
ذلك على يد فاسق لأنه مقدور في نفسه؛ فإن قيل: فهل من المقدور إظهار معجزة
على يد كاذب؟ قلنا: المعجزة مقرونة بالتحدي منه سبحانه نازلة منزلة قوله
صدقت وأنت رسول، وتصديق الكاذب محال لذاته وكل من قال له أنت رسولي صار
رسولا وخرج عن كونه كاذبا، فالجمع بين كونه كاذبا وبين ما ينزل منزلة قوله
أنت رسولي محال لأن معنى كونه كاذبا أنه ما قيل له أنت رسولي، ومعنى
المعجزة أنه قيل له أنت رسولي؛ فإن فعل الملك على ما ضربنا من المثال كقوله
أنت رسولي بالضرورة، فاستبان أن هذا غير مقدور لأنه محال والمحال لا قدرة
عليه. فهذا تمام هذا القطب ولنشرع في
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To send forth with a message; the core sense is dispatching an envoy with a commission
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Prophetic mission (risālah) as divine communication of what benefits or harms in the afterlife
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage for sending a messenger; metaphorical extension to divine commissioning
- Root: خ-ر-ق (kh-r-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To tear, rend, pierce through; hence breaking through the customary
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Miracle (muʿjizah) as that which ruptures the habitual order (ʿādah) as divine attestation
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal tearing of cloth; metaphorical for violating the norm of nature
- Root: غ-و-ي (gh-w-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To err, perish, be led astray from the right course
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine misguidance (ighwāʾ) as a theological problem concerning divine justice
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal deviation from the path; metaphorical for spiritual ruin
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs intricate conditional chains (law... fa-, in... fa-) and exceptive clauses (illā) to distinguish necessary from contingent divine acts, requiring careful parsing of protasis and apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: We affirm that the mission of the prophets is permissible (jāʾiz) — neither impossible (muḥāl) nor obligatory (wājib). The Muʿtazilites held it to be obligatory, and the refutation of their position has already preceded. The Brahmins held it to be impossible. The proof of its permissibility is that whenever the evidence has established that God most high is a speaker (mutakallim), and the evidence has established that He is powerful, incapable of being thwarted, to indicate the speech of the soul (kalām al-nafs) by creating words, sounds, written marks, or other indicators — and the evidence for the permissibility of sending messengers has been established — for we mean by this nothing other than that there subsists in the essence of God most high a report concerning what is beneficial in the afterlife and what is harmful, by virtue of the customary course (ʿādah), and there issues from Him an act that is an indication of that report to a person, and of His command to convey the report, and there issues from Him an act that breaks the customary order (khāriq li-l-ʿādah), conjoined with that person's claim to prophethood. None of this is impossible in itself, for it reduces to the speech of the soul and to the invention of what is an indication of that speech and what confirms the messenger. If one judges its impossibility on grounds of the ugly and the beautiful (al-istiqbāḥ wa al-istiḥsān), we have already uprooted this principle with respect to God most high. Nor can one claim the ugliness of sending a messenger on the principle of the ugly, for the Muʿtazilites, despite their commitment to that principle, did not deem this ugly. Thus, perceiving its ugliness is not necessary, nor is perceiving its impossibility in itself necessary; so a cause must be mentioned. The utmost that can be adduced against it consists of three doubts:

The first: Their saying — if the prophet were sent with what the intellects require, then the intellects are self-sufficient without him, and the mission of the messenger would be vain (ʿabath), and that is impossible for God; but if he were sent with what contradicts the intellects, then affirmation and acceptance would be impossible.

The second: That vanity is impossible because defining his truthfulness is impossible. For if God most high addressed creation directly with his confirmation and spoke to them openly, then there would be no need for a messenger; but if He did not address them directly, then the utmost is indicating his truthfulness by an act breaking the customary order — yet this is not distinguished from sorcery (siḥr), talismans (ṭilasmāt), and the wonders of special properties (khawāṣṣ), which are extraordinary relative to custom for those who do not know them. When they are equal in breaking custom, one is not secure from it, so no knowledge of truthfulness is attained.

The third: If the distinction between these and sorcery, talismans, and illusions is known, then from where is truthfulness known? Perhaps God most high intended to mislead us and lead us astray by confirming him; perhaps everything the prophet said would bring felicity is actually misery, and everything he said would bring misery is actually felicity — but God intended to drive us to destruction and misguide us through the prophet's speech. For misguidance (iḍlāl) and leading astray (ighwāʾ) are not impossible for God most high according to you, since the intellect neither deems good nor deems ugly. This is the strongest doubt, with which the Muʿtazilite should argue when seeking to impose the doctrine of the intellect's deeming ugly — for he says: If leading astray is not ugly, then the truthfulness of the messengers can never be known, nor can it be known that it is not misguidance.

The answer is that we say:

As for the first doubt, it is weak. For the prophet, peace be upon him, comes as an informant of what the intellects do not occupy themselves with knowing, but which they are competent to understand once known. For the intellect does not guide to what is beneficial and harmful among deeds, words, moral traits, and beliefs, nor does it distinguish between the miserable and the felicitous — just as it is not competent to grasp the special properties of medicines and drugs. But once known, it understands, affirms, and benefits from hearing, so it avoids destruction and seeks felicity — just as one benefits from the physician's speech in knowing the disease and the remedy. Then, just as the physician's truthfulness is known through circumstantial indications (qarāʾin al-aḥwāl) and other matters, so too the truthfulness of the messenger, peace be upon him, is inferred through miracles, indications, and states — so there is no difference.

As for the second doubt — the failure to distinguish the miracle from sorcery and illusion — it is not so. For no rational person has ever deemed it permissible that sorcery could reach the point of reviving the dead, turning the staff into a serpent, splitting the moon, parting the sea, curing the blind and the leper, and the like. The concise statement is: If this objector claims that everything God is powerful over is possible to achieve through sorcery, this is a claim known to be impossible by necessity. But if he distinguishes between the act of one group and the act of another, then he has conceived the confirmation of the messenger through what he knows is not sorcery; and the inquiry remains thereafter concerning the specific messengers, peace be upon them, and individual miracles — whether what they manifested is of the kind achievable by sorcery or not. Whenever doubt occurs therein, confirmation is not attained unless the prophet issued the challenge (taḥaddī) before an assembly of the greatest sorcerers, did not grant them a period for opposition, and they were unable to match it. But it is not our present purpose to examine individual miracles.

As for the third doubt — conceiving divine leading astray and the skepticism arising from that — we say: Whenever the aspect of the miracle's indication of the prophet's truthfulness is known, it is known that one is secure from that. This is by knowing prophethood and its meaning, and knowing the aspect of indication. We say: If a man issued a challenge before a king, in the presence of his troops, that he was the king's messenger to them, and that the king had made obedience to him obligatory upon them in the distribution of provisions and land grants, and they demanded proof while the king remained silent — and he said: "O king, if I am truthful in what I claim, then confirm me by rising from your throne three times consecutively and sitting contrary to your habit" — and the king rose immediately after his request three times consecutively, then sat — the attendees would necessarily know that he was the king's messenger before it even occurred to their minds whether this king's habit was to mislead or whether that was impossible in his case. Rather, even if the king said, "You have spoken truthfully; I have made you a messenger and an agent," they would know he was an agent and messenger. So when he violates custom by his act, that act is like his saying, "You are my messenger." This is an inaugural appointment, delegation, and commission — and falsehood is not conceivable in delegation; it is only conceivable in reportage. The knowledge that this is confirmation and delegation is necessary. For this reason, no one has denied the truthfulness of the prophets from this aspect; rather, they denied that what the prophets brought was extraordinary, attributing it to sorcery and deception — or they denied the existence of a speaking Lord, commanding, forbidding, confirming, and sending. But whoever acknowledges all of that and acknowledges that the miracle is the act of God most high attains necessary knowledge of confirmation.

If it is said: "Grant that they saw God most high with their own eyes and heard Him with their ears saying, 'This is My messenger, to inform you of the way of your felicity and misery' — what secures you that He did not mislead the messenger and the one sent to, informing of the miserable as felicitous and the felicitous as miserable? For that is not impossible if you do not affirm the intellect's deeming ugly. Rather, even if we suppose no messenger, but God most high said directly, openly, and by direct vision: 'Your salvation is in fasting, prayer, and alms; your destruction is in abandoning them' — by what do we know His truthfulness? Perhaps He deceives us to mislead and destroy us. For falsehood, according to you, is not ugly in itself; and even if it were ugly, what is ugly and unjust is not impossible for God most high — and in it is the destruction of all creation."

The answer: Falsehood is secured against. For it occurs only in speech, and the speech of God most high is not sound nor letter, such that deception could penetrate it. Rather, it is a meaning subsisting in His essence, exalted be He. So everything a human knows subsists in his essence as a report of what he knows, in accordance with his knowledge — and falsehood is not conceivable therein. Likewise in the case of God most high. In sum: falsehood in the speech of the soul is impossible, and in that is security from what they claimed. It has thus become clear that whenever an act is known to be the act of God most high, beyond the power of human beings, and is conjoined with the claim of prophethood, necessary knowledge of truthfulness is attained; and doubt arises only from doubting whether it is within human power or not. But once it is known to be the act of God most high, no room for doubt remains whatsoever.

If it is said: "Do you deem miracles of saints (karāmāt) permissible?" We say: People have differed on this; the truth is that it is permissible. For it reduces to God most high breaking custom at the supplication of a person or at his need — and that is not impossible in itself, for it is possible, and it does not lead to another impossibility. For it does not lead to the invalidation of the prophetic miracle, because the saintly miracle (karāmah) is an expression for what appears without being conjoined with a challenge (taḥaddī). If it is with a challenge, then we call it a miracle (muʿjizah), and it indicates by necessity the truthfulness of the challenger. If there is no claim, then its appearance at the hand of a sinner is permissible, because it is possible in itself.

If it is said: "Is it within divine power to manifest a miracle at the hand of a liar?" We say: The miracle, being conjoined with the challenge, is from Him, exalted be He, in the position of His saying, "You have spoken truthfully, and you are a messenger." Confirming a liar is impossible in itself. For anyone to whom He says, "You are My messenger," becomes a messenger and exits from being a liar. Thus, combining his being a liar with what is in the position of His saying, "You are My messenger," is impossible — because the meaning of his being a liar is that it was not said to him, "You are My messenger," and the meaning of the miracle is that it was said to him, "You are My messenger." For the king's act, on the example we gave, is necessarily like his saying, "You are my messenger." It has thus become evident that this is not within power, because it is impossible, and the impossible is not within power. This completes this pole (quṭb). Let us now proceed to —

### | إثبات نبوة نبينا محمد

صلى الله عليه وسلم وإثبات ما اخبر هو عنه والله أعلم.

### | القطب الرابع

إثبات نبوة نبينا محمد

### | صلى الله عليه وسلم وإثبات ما أخبر هو عنه

وفيه أربعة أبواب:

### | الباب الأول

: في اثبات نبوة نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم.
الباب الثاني: في بيان إن ما جاء به من الحشر والنشر والصراط والميزان
وعذاب القبر حق، وفيه مقدمة وفصلان.
الباب الثالث: فيه نظر في ثلاثة أطراف.
الباب الرابع: في بيان من يجب تكفيره من الفرق ومن لا يجب، والاشارة إلى
القوانين التي ينبغي أن يعول عليها في التكفير، وبه اختتام الكتاب.

### | الباب الأول

### | في اثبات نبوة نبينا محمد

### | صلى الله عليه وسلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "announcement of grave import" (inbāʾ); nabī derives from nabāʾ, signifying one divinely informed of unseen realities.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Prophethood (nubuwwah) is a divine bestowal (waḥy) conveying law and unseen knowledge, distinct from mere intellectual acquisition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes the prophetic office; metaphorical (majāz) extension to "one who informs" is secondary and non-technical.
- Root: ح-ش-ر (ḥ-sh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes gathering and driving forth (jamʿ wa sayq); al-ḥashr is the eschatological assembly of creation for reckoning.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, it is the divinely ordained resurrection (baʿth) and congregation at the Plain of Standing (mawqif).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical herding; metaphorical for the compelled gathering of souls before the Divine Decree.
- Root: ص-ر-ط (ṣ-r-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A loan-root (muʿarrab) meaning the straight path (al-ṭarīq al-wāḍiḥ); in eschatology, the bridge over Hell.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Ṣirāṭ is the manifest way of truth in this world and the literal bridge in the hereafter, both affirmed as real (ḥaqq).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physical bridge; metaphorical for the moral trial of passing over it.
- Root: م-ي-ز (m-y-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes separation and discrimination (tamyīz); al-mīzān is the instrument of weighing deeds.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Balance is the divine standard of justice (ʿadl) for appraising acts, affirmed as a true reality.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physical scale; metaphorical for the equitable measure of recompense.
- Root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root means covering (satr); kufr is covering the truth, and takfīr is the juridical declaration of unbelief.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Takfīr is a legal-theological judgment (ḥukm sharʿī) requiring precise criteria (ḍawābiṭ) to avoid excess (ghulūw) or negligence (taqṣīr).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for covering; metaphorical for veiling divine truth by denial or rejection.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Coordination) — When the author states "the Fourth Pole: Establishing the Prophethood..." and then repeats "Establishing the Prophethood..." with wa (and), the second clause is explanatory apposition (badal), reinforcing the topic without introducing a new subject. Also, the genitive construction (iḍāfah) in "Ithbāt nubuwwat nabiyyinā" (establishing the prophethood of our Prophet) requires the governed noun (muḍāf) to be indefinite in meaning but definite by annexation, yielding precise theological scope.
chapters.translation:
I say — and God is the Guide to what is correct:

### | Establishing the Prophethood of Our Prophet Muhammad — Peace and Blessings Upon Him — and Establishing What He Informs Of. And God Knows Best.

### | The Fourth Pole

Establishing the Prophethood of Our Prophet Muhammad — Peace and Blessings Upon Him — and Establishing What He Informs Of.

It comprises four chapters:

### | Chapter One

: On establishing the prophethood of our Prophet — Peace and Blessings Upon Him.
Chapter Two: On clarifying that what he brought concerning the Gathering (al-ḥashr), the Resurrection (al-nashr), the Bridge (al-ṣirāṭ), the Balance (al-mīzān), and the Punishment of the Grave (ʿadhāb al-qabr) is true — and it contains an introduction and two sections.
Chapter Three: It contains an examination of three aspects (aṭrāf).
Chapter Four: On clarifying which of the sects (al-firaq) must be declared unbelievers (takfīr) and which must not, and an indication of the legal principles (al-qawānīn) upon which one ought to rely in declaring unbelief (takfīr) — and with it the book concludes.

### | On Establishing the Prophethood of Our Prophet Muhammad

### | Peace and Blessings Upon Him

chapters.title_en: Establishing the Prophethood of Muhammad (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam) Against Three Sects
chapters.arabic_text:
وإنما نفتقر إلى إثبات نبوته، على الخصوص، وعلى ثلاثة فرق: الفرقة
الأولى، العيسوية: حيث ذهبوا إلى أنه رسول إلى العرب فقط لا إلى غيرهم،
وهذا ظاهر البطلان فإنهم اعترفوا بكونه رسولا حقا، ومعلوم أن الرسول لا
يكذب، وقد ادعى هو أنه رسول مبعوث إلى الثقلين، وبعث رسوله إلى كسرى وقيصر
وسائر ملوك العجم وتواتر ذلك منه فما قالوه محال متناقض.
الفرقة الثانية، اليهود: فإنهم انكروا صدقه لا بخصوص نظر فيه وفي
معجزاته، بل زعموا أنه لا نبي بعد موسى  عليه السلام، فأنكروا نبوة محمد
وعيسى عليهما السلام. فينبغي أن تثبت عليهم نبوة عيسى لأنه ربما يقصر فهمهم
عن درك إعجاز القرآن ولا يقصرون عن درك إعجاز إحياء الموتى وإبراء الأكمه
والأبرص فيقال لهم ما الذي حملكم على التفريق بين من يستدل على صدقه بإحياء
الموتى وبين من يستدل بقلب العصا ثعبانا؟ ولا يجدون إليه سبيلا البتة، إلا
أنهم ضلوا بشبهتين: إحداهما، قولهم: النسخ محال في نفسه لأنه يدل على البدء
والتغيير وذلك محال على الله تعالى، والثانية لفهم بعض الملحدة أن يقولوا:
قد قال موسى عليه السلام: عليكم بديني ما دامت السموات والأرض، وإنه قال
إني خاتم الأنبياء.
أما الشبهة الأولى فبطلانها بفهم النسخ، وهو عبارة عن الخطاب الدال على
ارتفاع الحكم الثابت المشروط استمراره بعد لحقوق خطاب يرفعه، وليس من
المحال أن يقول السيد لعبده قم مطلقا، ولا يبين له مدة القيام، وهو يعلم أن
القيام مقتضى منه إلى وقت بقاء مصلحته في القيام، ويعلم مدة مصلحته ولكن لا
ينبه عليها، ويفهم العبد أنه مأمور بالقيام مطلقا وأن الواجب الاستمرار
عليه أبدا إلا أن يخاطبه السيد بالقعود؛ فإذا خاطبه بالقعود قعد ولم يتوهم
بالسيد أنه بدا له أو ظهرت له مصلحة كان لا يعرفها، والآن قد عرفها، بل
يجوز أن يكون قد عرف مدة مصلحة القيام وعرف أن الصلاح في أن لا ينبه العبد
عليها ويطلق الأمر له إطلاقا حتى يستمر على الامتثال، ثم إذا تغيرت مصلحته
أمره بالقعود، فهكذا ينبغي أن يفهم اختلاف
أحكام الشرائع. فإن ورود النبي ليس بناسخ لشرع من قبله بمجرد بعثته، ولا
في معظم الأحكام، ولكن في بعض الأحكام كتغير قبلة وتحليل محرم وغير ذلك،
وهذه المصالح تختلف بالأعصار والأحوال فليس فيه ما يدل على التغير ولا على
الاستبانة بعد الجهل ولا على التناقض. ثم هذا إنما يستمر لليهود إذ لو
اعتقدوا أنه لم يكن شريعة من لدن آدم إلى زمن موسى لم ينكروا وجود نوح
وإبراهيم وشرعهما، ولا يتميزون فيه عمن ينكر  نبوة موسى وشرعه وكل ذلك إنكار
ما علم على القطع بالتواتر.
وأما الشبهة الثانية فسخيفة من وجهين. أحدهما، أنه لو صح ما قالوه عن
موسى لما ظهرت المعجزات على يد عيسى، فإن ذلك تصديق بالضرورة، فكيف يصدق
الله بالمعجزة من يكذب موسى وهو أيضا مصدق له، أفتنكرون معجزة عيسى وجودا
أو تنكرون إحياء الموتى دليلا على صدق المتحدي؟ فإن أنكروا شيئا منهم لزمهم
في شرع موسى لزوما لا يجدون عنه محيصا، وإذا اعترفوا به لزمهم تكذيب من نقل
إليهم من موسى عليه السلام قوله إني خاتم الأنبياء. والثاني: أن هذه الشبهة
إنما لقنوها بعد بعثة نبينا محمد عليه السلام وبعد وفاته، ولو كانت صحيحة
لاحتج اليهود بها وقد حملوا بالسيف على الاسلام، وكان رسولنا عليه السلام
مصدقا بموسى عليه السلام وحاكما على اليهود بالتوراة في حكم الرجم وغيره،
فلا عرض عليه من التوارة ذلك، وما الذي صرفهم عنه ومعلوم قطعا أن اليهود لم
يحتجوا به لأن ذلك لو كان لكان مفحما لا جواب عنه ولتواتر نقله، ومعلوم
أنهم لم يتركوه مع القدرة عليه ولقد كانوا يحرصون على الطعن في شرعه بكل
ممكن حماية لدمائهم وأموالهم ونسائهم، فإذا ثبت عليهم نبوة عيسى أثبتنا
نبوة نبينا عليه السلام بما نثبتها على النصارى.
الفرقة الثالثة، وهم يجوزون النسخ ولكنهم ينكرون نبوة نبينا من حيث أنهم
ينكرون معجزته في القرآن. وفي إثبات نبوته بالمعجزة طريقتان:
الطريقة الأولى، التمسك بالقرآن، فإنا نقول: لا معنى للمعجزة إلا ما
يقترن بتحدي النبي عند استشهاده على صدقه على وجه يعجز الخلق عن معارضته،
وتحديه على العرب مع شغفهم بالفصاحة وإغراقهم فيها متواتر، وعدم المعارضة
معلوم، إذ لو كان لظهر، فإن أرذل الشعراء لما تحدوا بشعرهم وعورضوا ظهرت
المعارضات والمناقضات الجارية بينهم، فإذا لا يمكن إنكار تحديه بالقرآن ولا
يمكن إنكار اقتدار العرب على طريق الفصاحة ولا يمكن انكار حرصهم على دفع
نبوته بكل ممكن حماية لدينهم ودمهم ومالهم وتخلصا من سطوة المسلمين وقهرهم،
ولا يمكن إنكار عجزهم
لأنهم  لو قدروا لفعلوا، فإن العادة قاضية بالضرورة بأن القادر على دفع
الهلاك عن نفسه يشتغل بدفعه، ولو فعلوا لظهر ذلك ونقل. فهذه مقدمات بعضها
بالتواتر وبعضها بجاري العادات وكل ذلك مما يورث اليقين فلا حاجة إلى
التطويل. وبمثل هذا الطريق تثبت نبوة عيسى ولا يقدر النصراني على إنكار شيء
من ذلك؛ فإنه يمكن أن يقابل بعيسى فينكر تحديه بالنبوة أو استشهاده باحياء
الموتى أو وجود إحياء الموتى أو عدم المعارضة أو يقال عورض ولم يظهر، وكل
ذلك مجاحدات لا يقدر عليها المعترف بأصل النبوات، فإن قيل: ما وجه إعجاز
القرآن؟ قلنا الجزالة والفصاحة مع النظم العجيب والمنهاج الخارج عن مناهج
كلام العرب في خطبهم وأشعارهم وسائر صنوف كلامهم، والجمع بين هذا النظم
وهذه الجزالة معجز خارج عن مقدور البشر، نعم ربما يرى للعرب أشعار وخطب حكم
فيها بالجزالة، وربما ينقل عن بعض من قصد المعارضة مراعاة هذا النظم بعد
تعلمه من القرآن، ولكن من غير جزالة بل مع ركاكة كما يحكى عن ترهات مسيلمة
الكذاب حيث قال: الفيل وما أدراك ما الفيل له ذنب وثيل وخرطوم طويل. فهذا
وأمثاله ربما يقدر عليه مع ركاكة يستغثها الفصحاء ويستهزؤون بها، وأما
جزالة القرآن فقد قضى كافة العرب منها العجب ولم ينقل عن واحد منهم تشبث
بطعن في فصاحته، فهذا إذا معجز وخارج عن مقدور البشر من هذين الوجهين، أعني
من اجتماع هذين الوجهين، فإن قيل: لعل العرب اشتغلت بالمحاربة والقتال فلم
تعرج على معارضة القرآن ولو قصدت لقدرت عليه، أو منعتها العوائق عن
الاشتغال به، والجواب أن ما ذكروه هوس، فإن دفع تحدي المتحدي بنظم كلام
أهون من الدفع بالسيف مع ما جرى على العرب من المسلمين بالأسر والقتل
والسبي وشن الغارات، ثم ما ذكروه غير دافع غرضنا، فإن انصرافهم عن المعارضة
لم يكن إلا بصرف من الله تعالى، والصرف عن المقدور المعتاد من أعظم
المعجزات، فلو قال نبي آية صدقي أني في هذا اليوم أحرك أصبعي ولا يقدر أحد
من البشر  على معارضتي، فلم يعارضه أحد في ذلك اليوم، ثبت صدقه، وكان فقد
قدرتهم على الحركة مع سلامة الأعضاء من أعظم المعجزات. وإن فرض وجود القدرة
ففقد داعيتهم وصرفهم عن المعارضة من أعظم المعجزات، مهما كانت حاجتهم ماسة
إلى الدفع باستيلاء النبي على رقابهم وأموالهم، وذلك كله معلوم على
الضرورة. فهذا طريق تقدير نبوته على النصارى، ومهما تشبثوا بانكار شيء من
هذه الأمور الجليلة فلا تشتغل إلا بمعارضتهم بمثله في معجزات عيسى عليه
السلام.
الطريقة الثانية: أن تثبت نبوته بجملة من الأفعال الخارقة للعادات التي
ظهرت عليه، كانشقاق القمر، ونطق العجماء، وتفجر الماء من بين أصابعه،
وتسبيح الحصى في كفه، وتكثير الطعام القليل، وغيره من خوارق العادات، وكل
ذلك دليل على صدقه. فإن قيل: آحاد هذه الوقائع لم يبلغ نقلها مبلغ التواتر.
قلنا: ذلك أيضا إن سلم فلا يقدح في العرض مهما كان المجموع بالغا مبلغ
التواتر، وهذا كما أن شجاعة علي رضوان الله عليه وسخاوة حاتم معلومان
بالضرورة على القطع تواترا، وآحاد تلك الوقائع لم تثبت تواترا، ولكن يعلم
من مجموع الآحاد على القطع ثبوت صفة الشجاعة والسخاوة، فكذلك هذه الأحوال
العجيبة بالغة جملتها مبلغ التواتر، لا يستريب فيها مسلم أصلا. فإن قال
قائل من النصارى: هذه الأمور لم تتواتر عندي لا جملتها ولا آحادها. فيقال:
ولو انحاز يهودي إلى قطر من الأقطار ولم يخالط النصارى وزعم أنه لم تتواتر
عنده معجزات عيسى، وإن تواترت فعلى لسان النصارى وهم مهتمون به، فبماذا
ينفصلون عنه؟ ولا انفصال عنه إلا أن يقال: ينبغي أن يخالط القوم الذين
تواتر ذلك بينهم حتى يتواتر ذلك إليك، فإن الأصم لا تتواتر عنده الأخبار،
وكذا المتصامم، فهذا أيضا عذرنا عند إنكار واحد منهم التواتر على هذا
الوجه.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of "announcement" (inbāʾ) — the one who conveys a momentous report; nabī is the one informed by God.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Prophethood (nubuwwa) as divinely-bestowed information and mission (risāla), entailing veracity (ṣidq) as a logical necessity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) for the prophetic office; metaphorically (majāz) never applied to pretenders in this argumentative context.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Protasis Emphasis (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — the structure "fa-in qīl... qulnā" governs the dialectical sequence, marking each objection and response as a complete syntactic unit.
chapters.translation:
I say: We need to establish his prophethood, specifically, against three sects.

The first sect is the ʿĪsawiyya, who held that he was a messenger to the Arabs only, not to others. This is manifestly false, for they acknowledged him to be a true messenger, and it is known that a messenger does not lie. Yet he himself claimed to be a messenger sent to the two weighty kinds (al-thaqalayn: jinn and mankind), and he dispatched his envoy to Chosroes and Caesar and the rest of the kings of the non-Arabs, and this was transmitted from him by recurrent report (tawātur). So what they said is impossible and self-contradictory.

The second sect is the Jews, for they denied his truthfulness not by specific examination of him and his miracles, but rather claimed that there is no prophet after Moses (upon him be peace). Thus they denied the prophethood of Muhammad and Jesus (upon them both be peace). So one ought to establish against them the prophethood of Jesus, because perhaps their understanding falls short of grasping the inimitability (iʿjāz) of the Qurʾān, but they do not fall short of grasping the inimitability of reviving the dead and curing the blind and the leper. So it is said to them: What drove you to differentiate between one whose truthfulness is evidenced by reviving the dead and one whose truthfulness is evidenced by turning the staff into a serpent? They find no way out of this at all, except that they went astray through two ambiguities (shubhatayn):

One of them is their saying: Abrogation (naskh) is impossible in itself, because it indicates a change of mind (badāʾ) and alteration, and that is impossible for God Most High.

The second is their grasping at what some heretics (mulḥida) said: Moses (upon him be peace) said: "Hold fast to my religion as long as the heavens and the earth endure," and he said: "I am the seal of the prophets."

As for the first ambiguity, its falsity is shown by understanding abrogation (naskh). It is an expression for a discourse indicating the lifting of an established ruling whose continuance is conditioned, after the arrival of a discourse that lifts it. It is not impossible for a master to say to his slave: "Stand," absolutely, without specifying the duration of standing, while he knows that standing is required from him until the time his benefit lies in standing, and he knows the duration of that benefit but does not draw attention to it. The slave understands that he is commanded to stand absolutely and that the obligation is to continue upon it forever, unless the master addresses him with "Sit." So when he addresses him with "Sit," he sits, and does not suppose of the master that he changed his mind (badā lahu) or that a benefit appeared to him which he had not known and now has known. Rather, it is permissible that he had known the duration of the benefit of standing and knew that the sound course was not to alert the slave to it, but to give him the command absolutely, so that he persists in compliance. Then when his benefit changed, he commanded him to sit. Likewise should one understand the variation of the rulings of the religious laws (sharāʾiʿ). For the advent of a prophet is not an abrogation of the law of one before him merely by his being sent, nor in most rulings, but only in some rulings, such as the change of the qibla and the making lawful of what was forbidden, and other such matters. These benefits vary with the ages and circumstances, so there is nothing in this indicating alteration, nor indicating becoming clear after ignorance, nor indicating contradiction.

Then this [argument] only holds against the Jews, for if they believed that there was no law from the time of Adam until the time of Moses, they would not deny the existence of Noah and Abraham and their laws. And they are not distinguished in this from one who denies the prophethood of Moses and his law — all of which is denial of what is known with certainty by recurrent transmission (tawātur).

As for the second ambiguity, it is flimsy in two respects. First: If what they reported from Moses were true, the miracles would not have appeared at the hand of Jesus, for that would be a confirmation by necessity. So how could God confirm through a miracle one who belies Moses, while he too confirms him? Do you deny the miracle of Jesus in its existence, or do you deny that reviving the dead is evidence of the truthfulness of the one who issues the challenge (muttaḥaddī)? If they deny any of these, the same [denial] applies to the law of Moses with a necessity from which they find no escape. And if they acknowledge it, then they are compelled to belie those who transmitted to them from Moses (upon him be peace) his saying: "I am the seal of the prophets."

Second: This ambiguity was only instilled in them after the mission of our Prophet Muhammad (upon him be peace) and after his death. Had it been sound, the Jews would have argued with it when they were driven by the sword to Islam, while our Messenger (upon him be peace) confirmed Moses (upon him be peace) and judged over the Jews by the Torah in the matter of stoning and other matters. Yet none of them presented that from the Torah to him. What turned them away from it? It is known with certainty that the Jews did not argue with it, for had they done so, it would have been an irrefutable argument with no answer, and its transmission would have been recurrent. And it is known that they did not abandon it while able [to use it], for they were eager to attack his law by every possible means, to protect their blood, wealth, and women. So when the prophethood of Jesus is established against them, we establish the prophethood of our Prophet (upon him be peace) by the same means by which we establish it against the Christians.

The third sect: They permit abrogation (naskh) but deny the prophethood of our Prophet in that they deny his miracle in the Qurʾān. In establishing his prophethood by the miracle, there are two methods:

The first method is adherence to the Qurʾān. For we say: The meaning of "miracle" (muʿjiza) is nothing other than what is conjoined with the prophet's challenge (taḥaddī) when he summons evidence of his truthfulness, in a manner whereby creation is incapable of opposing it. His challenge to the Arabs, given their passion for eloquence (faṣāḥa) and their immersion in it, is recurrently transmitted (mutawātir). The absence of opposition is known, for had it occurred, it would have appeared. For when the meanest poets challenged with their poetry and were opposed, the counter-poems and refutations exchanged among them appeared. So it is impossible to deny his challenge by the Qurʾān, impossible to deny the Arabs' power in the way of eloquence, impossible to deny their eagerness to repel his prophethood by every possible means — to protect their religion, blood, and wealth, and to escape the domination and coercion of the Muslims — and impossible to deny their incapacity, for had they been able, they would have done it. For custom (ʿāda) necessarily dictates that one who is able to repel destruction from himself busies himself with repelling it. And had they done it, it would have appeared and been transmitted. These premises are some by recurrent transmission (tawātur) and some by the course of custom (jarayān al-ʿādāt), and all of this yields certainty, so there is no need for elaboration.

By this same method the prophethood of Jesus is established, and the Christian cannot deny any of it. For he could be countered with Jesus, and one might deny his challenge to prophethood, or his summoning evidence by reviving the dead, or the existence of the revival of the dead, or the absence of opposition — or say: "He was opposed but it did not appear." All of that is obstinate denial (mujāḥada) which one who acknowledges the principle of prophethoods cannot sustain.

If it is said: What is the aspect of the inimitability (iʿjāz) of the Qurʾān? We say: Its grandeur of diction (jazāla) and eloquence (faṣāḥa), with its wondrous composition (naẓm) and its course that departs from the courses of Arab speech in their orations, poems, and all their other kinds of discourse. The combination of this composition and this grandeur is a miracle beyond the power of humans. Yes, one may find for the Arabs poems and orations judged to have grandeur, and one may transmit from some who intended opposition a regard for this composition after learning it from the Qurʾān, but without grandeur — rather with feebleness (rakāka), as is related of the absurdities of Musaylima the Liar, when he said: "The elephant — and what will make you know what the elephant is? It has a tail and a trunk and a long proboscis." This and its like one might perhaps manage, with a feebleness that the eloquent find repulsive and mock. As for the grandeur of the Qurʾān, all the Arabs were struck with wonder at it, and no transmission from any one of them exists of clinging to an attack on its eloquence. So it is a miracle, beyond the power of humans, in these two respects — that is, in the conjunction of these two respects.

If it is said: Perhaps the Arabs were occupied with warfare and fighting and did not turn to opposing the Qurʾān, and had they intended it they would have been able; or obstacles prevented them from occupying themselves with it — the answer is that what they mentioned is nonsense. For repelling the challenge of one who challenges with the composition of speech is easier than repelling with the sword, given what befell the Arabs at the hands of the Muslims — captivity, killing, plundering, and launching raids. Moreover, what they mentioned does not repel our purpose. For their turning away from opposition was only by a turning-aside (ṣarf) from God Most High, and the turning-aside from what is customary and within power is among the greatest miracles. If a prophet said: "The sign of my truthfulness is that on this day I move my finger and no human is able to oppose me," and no one opposed him that day, his truthfulness is established, and the loss of their power to move, with sound limbs, would be among the greatest miracles. And if power is assumed to exist, then the loss of their motive and their being turned aside from opposition is among the greatest miracles, whenever their need to repel was pressing, given the prophet's domination over their necks and wealth. All of that is known by necessity. This is the method of establishing his prophethood against the Christians. And whenever they cling to denying any of these evident matters, do not occupy yourself except by countering them with the like of it in the miracles of Jesus (upon him be peace).

The second method: That his prophethood be established by a body of superordinary acts (khawāriq al-ʿādāt) that appeared from him — such as the splitting of the moon, the speech of the dumb animal, the gushing of water from between his fingers, the glorification of the pebbles in his palm, the multiplication of scant food, and other superordinary acts. All of that is evidence of his truthfulness.

If it is said: The individual reports of these events did not reach the level of recurrent transmission (tawātur). We say: Even if that is granted, it does not harm the purpose as long as the totality reaches the level of recurrent transmission. This is like the courage of ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him) and the generosity of Ḥātim — both are known by necessity with certainty through recurrent transmission, while the individual reports of those events are not established by recurrent transmission. Yet from the totality of the individual reports, the possession of the qualities of courage and generosity is known with certainty. Likewise these wondrous states, in their totality, reach the level of recurrent transmission; no Muslim doubts them at all.

If a Christian says: These matters have not reached me by recurrent transmission, neither in their totality nor in their individual reports — it is said to him: If a Jew withdrew to a remote region and did not mix with Christians, and claimed that the miracles of Jesus had not reached him by recurrent transmission — and if they did reach him, it was on the tongues of Christians who are partisan to him — how would they extricate themselves from him? There is no extrication from him except by saying: He ought to mix with the people among whom that is recurrently transmitted, so that it becomes recurrently transmitted to him. For the deaf man does not have reports transmitted to him recurrently, and likewise the one who feigns deafness. This too is our excuse when one of them denies recurrent transmission in this manner.

### | الباب الثاني

### | في بيان وجوب التصديق بأمور

### | ورد بها الشرع وقضى بجوازها العقل

وفيه مقدمة وفصلان، أما المقدمة: فهو أن ما لا يعلم بالضرورة ينقسم إلى
ما يعلم بدليل العقل دون الشرع، وإلى ما يعلم بالشرع دون العقل، وإلى  ما
يعلم بهما. أما المعلوم بدليل العقل دون الشرع فهو حدث العالم ووجود المحدث
وقدرته وعلمه وارادته، فإن كل ذلك ما لم يثبت لم يثبت الشرع، إذ الشرع يبنى
على الكلام فإن لم يثبت كلام النفس لم يثبت الشرع. فكل ما يتقدم في الرتبة
على كلام النفس يستحيل إثباته بكلام النفس وما يستند إليه ونفس الكلام أيضا
فيما اخترناه لا يمكن اثباته بالشرع. ومن المحققين من تكلف ذلك وادعاه كما
سبقت الاشارة إليه.
وأما المعلوم بمجرد السمع فتخصيص أحد الجائزين بالوقوع فإن ذلك من موافق
العقول، وإنما يعرف من الله تعالى بوحي والهام ونحن نعلم من الوحي إليه
بسماع كالحشر والنشر والثواب والعقاب وأمثالهما، وأما المعلوم بهما فكل ما
هو واقع في مجال العقل ومتأخر في الرتبة عن إثبات كلام الله تعالى كمسألة
الرؤية وانفراد الله تعالى بخلق الحركات والأغراض كلها وما يجري هذا
المجرى، ثم كلما ورد السمع به ينظر، فإن كان العقل مجوزا له وجب التصديق به
قطعا إن كانت الأدلة السمعية قاطعة في متنها ومستندها لا يتطرق إليها
احتمال، وجب التصديق بها ظنا إن كانت ظنية، فإن وجوب التصديق باللسان
والقلب عمل يبنى على الأدلة الظنية كسائر الأعمال فنحن نعلم قطعا إنكار
الصحابة على من يدعي كون العبد خالقا لشيء من الأشياء وعرض من الأعراض،
وكانوا ينكرون ذلك بمجرد قوله تعالى " خالق كل شيء " ومعلوم أنه عام قابل
للتخصيص فلا يكون عمومه إلا مظنونا، إنما صارت المسألة قطعية بالبحث على
الطرق العقلية التي ذكرناها، ونعلم أنهم كانوا ينكرون ذلك قبل البحث عن
الطرق العقلية ولا ينبغي أن يعتقد بهم أنهم لم يلتفتوا إلى المدارك الظنية
إلا في الفقهيات بل اعتبروها أيضا في التصديقات الاعتقادية والقولية.
وأما ما قضى العقل باستحالته فيجب فيه تأويل ما ورد السمع به ولا يتصور
أن يشمل السمع على قاطع مخالف للمعقول، وظواهر أحاديث التشبيه أكثرها غير
صحيحة، والصحيح منها ليس بقاطع بل هو قابل للتأويل، فإن توقف العقل في شيء
من ذلك  فلم يقض فيه باستحالة ولا جواز وجب التصديق أيضا لأدلة السمع فيكفي
في وجوب التصديق انفكاك العقل عن القضاء بالإحالة، وليس يشترط اشتماله على
القضاء لتجويز، وبين الرتبتين فرق ربما يزل ذهن البليد حتى لا يدرك الفرق
بين قول القائل: اعلم أن الأمر جائز، وبين قوله: لا أدري إنه محال أم جائز،
وبينهما ما بين السماء والأرض، إذ الأول جائز على الله تعالى والثاني غير
جائز، فإن الأول معرفة بالجواز والثاني عدم معرفة بالاحالة، ووجوب التصديق
جائز في القسمين جميعا فهذه هي المقدمة.

### | أما الفصل الأول ففي

### | بيان قضاء العقل بما جاء الشرع به

### | من الحشر والنشر وعذاب القبر والصراط والميزان
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Truthfulness, veracity; firmness in speech and belief; the opposite of falsehood (kidhb)
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Taṣdīq (affirmation) as the heart's assent to a proposition, distinct from mere verbal utterance; the cognitive act of judging something as true
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — affirming correspondence between belief and reality; metaphorical (majāz) — verbal affirmation without inner conviction
- Root: ج-و-ز (j-w-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Passing through, traversing; permissibility; what is not barred
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Jawāz (possibility) as the mind's judgment that a thing is not impossible — the middle category between necessity (wujūb) and impossibility (istiḥālah)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — permissibility in action; metaphorical — rational possibility (tajwīz al-ʿaql) as the absence of any proof of impossibility
- Root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Hearing; that which is transmitted by auditory reception
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Al-Samʿ (revelation) as the authoritative source of knowledge transmitted through prophets, contrasted with ʿaql (reason)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the physical sense of hearing; metaphorical — the entire body of transmitted revelation (al-samʿiyyāt)
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taqdīm wa-Taʾkhīr (Fronting and Delaying) — The fronting of "mā lā yuʿlamu bi-ḍarūrah" (what is not known necessarily) establishes the exhaustive division (taqsīm) that follows, while the delayed predicates (khabar) in each clause carry the burden of the classification.
chapters.translation:
I say: The second chapter concerns the exposition of the obligation to affirm matters which revelation (al-sharʿ) has conveyed and which reason (al-ʿaql) has judged to be possible.

This chapter comprises an introduction (muqaddimah) and two sections (faṣlān).

As for the introduction: Know that whatever is not known by necessity (ḍarūrah) divides into three categories: (1) that which is known by a rational proof (dalīl al-ʿaql) without recourse to revelation; (2) that which is known by revelation without recourse to reason; and (3) that which is known by both.

As for what is known by rational proof without revelation — it is the temporal origination of the world (ḥudūth al-ʿālam), the existence of the Originator (wujūd al-muḥdith), His power (qudrah), His knowledge (ʿilm), and His will (irādah). For none of these, if unestablished, would establish revelation itself, since revelation is built upon the [divine] speech (al-kalām). For if the speech of the soul (kalām al-nafs) is not established, revelation is not established. Thus, everything that precedes in rank the speech of the soul cannot possibly be established by the speech of the soul or by what depends upon it; and the speech itself, in what we have chosen [as our doctrine], cannot be established by revelation. Some among the verifiers (al-muḥaqqiqīn) have undertaken this [task] and claimed it, as was previously indicated.

As for what is known by mere audition (al-samʿ) alone — it is the specification (takhṣīṣ) of one of two possible things as actually occurring. For this is among what the intellects deem permissible (min muwāfiq al-ʿuqūl); it is known only from God — exalted be He — through revelation (waḥy) and inspiration (ilhām). And we know of the revelation to [the prophets] through hearing, such as the Resurrection and the Gathering (al-ḥashr wa-al-nashr), reward and punishment (al-thawāb wa-al-ʿiqāb), and their like.

As for what is known by both — it is everything that falls within the domain of reason and is posterior in rank to the establishment of God's speech — exalted be He — such as the question of the Beatific Vision (al-ruʾyah), God's exclusive creation of all movements and accidents (al-aʿrāḍ), and whatever runs in this course.

Then, whenever revelation conveys something, one examines it: if reason deems it possible, then affirmation of it becomes obligatory (wājib) definitively (qaṭʿan) if the scriptural evidences (al-adillah al-samʿiyyah) are conclusive (qāṭiʿah) in their text (matn) and chain (mustanad), with no possibility of [interpretive] doubt reaching them. If they are probable (ẓanniyyah), affirmation becomes obligatory as a matter of probable belief (ẓannan). For the obligation of affirmation by tongue and heart is an act (ʿamal) built upon probable evidences, just like other acts [of worship].

We know with certainty that the Companions (al-ṣaḥābah) rejected the claim of anyone who asserted that a servant is the creator (khāliq) of any thing whatsoever or of any accident whatsoever. They rejected this merely by virtue of His saying — exalted be He: {«خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ»} ("Creator of all things") [Q. 13:16]. And it is known that this [verse] is general (ʿāmm) and susceptible to specification (takhṣīṣ), so its generality is only probable. The matter only became definitive through investigation of the rational methods (al-ṭuruq al-ʿaqliyyah) which we have mentioned. And we know that they rejected this before investigating the rational methods. Nor should one believe of them that they paid no heed to probable sources of knowledge (al-madārik al-ẓanniyyah) except in jurisprudential matters (al-fiqhiyyāt); rather, they considered them also in doctrinal and verbal affirmations (al-taṣdīqāt al-iʿtiqādiyyah wa-al-qawliyyah).

As for what reason has judged to be impossible (istiḥālah), whatever revelation conveys regarding it must be interpreted allegorically (taʾwīl). It is inconceivable that revelation should contain something conclusive that contradicts the rational [judgment]. And the apparent meanings (ẓawāhir) of the traditions of anthropomorphism (aḥādīth al-tashbīh) — most of them are not authentic (ṣaḥīḥah); and what is authentic among them is not conclusive but rather susceptible to allegorical interpretation.

If reason remains undecided regarding something — neither judging it impossible nor deeming it possible — then affirmation is also obligatory on account of the scriptural evidences. For the mere fact that reason is free from any judgment of impossibility suffices for the obligation of affirmation; it is not required that reason include a judgment of possibility. Between these two ranks there is a difference — and perhaps the mind of the dullard may slip such that he fails to perceive the difference between one who says: "Know that the matter is possible," and one who says: "I do not know whether it is impossible or possible." Between the two is [a distance] like that between heaven and earth. For the first is permissible regarding God — exalted be He — while the second is not permissible. The first is a knowledge of possibility (maʿrifah bi-al-jawāz); the second is an absence of knowledge of impossibility (ʿadam maʿrifah bi-al-istiḥālah). And the obligation of affirmation holds in both categories alike. This, then, is the introduction.

As for the first section — it concerns the exposition of reason's judgment regarding what revelation has brought concerning the Resurrection and the Gathering (al-ḥashr wa-al-nashr), the punishment of the grave (ʿadhāb al-qabr), the Bridge (al-ṣirāṭ), and the Balance (al-mīzān).

chapters.title_en: On the Resurrection, the Torment of the Grave, the Balance, and the Path (Ṣirāṭ)
chapters.arabic_text:
أما الحشر فيعنى به إعادة الخلق وقد دلت عليه القواطع الشرعية، وهو ممكن
بدليل الابتداء. فإن الاعادة خلق ثان ولا فرق بينه وبين الابتداء وإنما
يسمى إعادة بالاضافة إلى الابتداء السابق، والقادر على الانشاء والابتداء
قادر على الاعادة وهو المعني بقوله: قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة فإن قيل
فماذا تقولون: أتعدم الجواهر والأعراض ثم يعادان جميعا، أو تعدم الأعراض
دون الجواهر وإنما تعاد الأعراض؟ قلنا: كل ذلك ممكن وليس في الشرع دليل
قاطع على تعيين أحد هذه الممكنات. وأحد الوجهين أن تنعدم الأعراض ويبقى جسم
الانسان متصورا بصورة التراب مثلا، فتكون قد زالت منه الحياة واللون
والرطوبة والتركيب والهيئة وجملة من الأعراض، ويكون معنى إعادتها أن تعاد
إليها تلك الأعراض بعينها وتعاد إليها أمثالها، فإن العرض عندنا لا يبقى
والحياة عرض والموجود عندنا في كل ساعة عرض آخر، والانسان هو ذلك الانسان
باعتبار جسمه فإنه واحد لا باعتبار أعراضه، فإن كل عرض يتجدد هو غير الآخر،
فليس من شرط الإعادة فرض إعادة الأعراض، وإنما ذكرنا هذا لمصير بعض الأصحاب
إلى استحالة إعادة الأعراض، وذلك باطل، ولكن القول في إبطاله يطول ولا حاجة
إليه في غرضنا هذا. والوجه الآخر أن تعدم الأجسام أيضا ثم تعاد الأجسام بأن
تخترع. مرة ثانية،
فإن قيل: فيم يتميز المعاد عن مثل الأول؟ وما  معنى قولكم أن المعاد هو
عين الأول ولم يبق للمعدوم عين حتى تعاد؟ قلنا: المعدوم منقسم في علم الله
إلى ما سبق له وجود وإلى ما لم يسبق له وجود، كما أن العدم في الأزل ينقسم
إلى ما سيكون له وجود وإلى ما علم الله تعالى أنه لا يوجد؛ فهذا الانقسام
في علم الله لا سبيل إلى انكاره، والعلم شامل والقدرة واسعة، فمعنى الإعادة
أن نبذل بالوجود العدم الذي سبق له الوجود، ومعنى المثل أن يخترع الوجود
لعدم لم يسبق له وجود، فهذا معنى الإعادة، ومهما قدر الجسم باقيا ورد الأمر
إلى تجديد أعراض تماثل الأول حصل تصديق الشرع ووقع الخلاص عن إشكال الإعادة
وتمييز المعاد عن المثل، وقد أطنبنا في هذه المسألة في كتاب التهافت،
وسلكنا في إبطال مذهبهم تقرير بقاء النفس التي هي غير متحيز عندهم وتقدير
عود تدبيرها إلى البدن سواء كان ذلك البدن هو عين جسم الانسان أو غيره،
وذلك إلزام لا يوافق ما نعتقده؛ فإن ذلك الكتاب مصنف لابطال مذهبهم لا
لاثبات المذهب الحق، ولكنهم لما قدروا أن الانسان هو ما هو باعتبار نفسه
وأن اشتغاله بتدبير كالعارض له والبدن آلة لهم، ألزمناهم بعد اعتقادهم بقاء
النفس وجوب التصديق بالاعادة وذلك برجوع النفس إلى تدبير بدن من الأبدان،
والنظر الآن في تحقيق هذا الفصل ينجر إلى البحث عن الروح والنفس والحياة
وحقائقها، ولا تحتمل المعتقدات التغلغل إلى هذه الغايات في المعقولات، فما
ذكرناه كاف في بيان الاقتصاد في الاعتقاد للتصديق بما جاء به الشرع، وأما
عذاب القبر فقد دلت عليه قواطع الشرع إذ تواتر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
وعن الصحابة رضي الله عنهم بالاستعاذة منه في الأدعية واشتهر قوله عند
المرور بقبرين: إنهما ليعذبان ودل عليه قوله تعالى " وحاق بآل فرعون سوء
العذاب النار يعرضون عليها غدوا وعشيا " الآية، وهو ممكن، فيجب التصديق به.
ووجه إمكانه ظاهر، وإنما تنكره المعتزلة من حيث يقولون إنا نرى شخص الميت
مشاهدة وهو غير معذب وإن الميت  ربما تفترسه السباع وتأكله، وهذا هوس؛ أما
مشاهدة الشخص فهو مشاهدة لظواهر الجسم والمدرك للعقاب جزء من القلب أو من
الباطن كيف كان وليس من ضرورة العذاب ظهور حركة في ظاهر البدن، بل الناظر
إلى ظاهر النائم لا يشاهد ما يدركه النائم من اللذة عند الاحتلام ومن الألم
عند تخيل الضرب وغيره، ولو انتبه النائم وأخبر عن مشاهداته وآلامه ولذاته
من لم يجر له عهد بالنوم لبادر إلى الانكار اغترارا بسكون ظاهر جسمه،
كمشاهدة إنكار المعتزلة لعذاب القبر وأما الذي تأكله السباع فغاية ما في
الباب أن يكون بطن السبع قبرا، فاعادة الحياة إلى جزء يدرك العذاب ممكن،
فما كل متألم يدرك الألم من جميع بدنه، وأما سؤال منكر ونكير فحق، والتصديق
به واجب لورود الشرع به وامكانه، فإن ذلك لا يستدعي منهما إلا تفهيما بصوت
أو بغير صوت، ولا يستدعي منه إلا فهما، ولا يستدعي الفهم إلا
حياة، والإنسان لا يفهم بجميع بدنه بل بجزء من باطن قلبه، واحياء جزء
يفهم السؤال ويجيب ممكن مقدور عليه، فيبقى قول القائل إنا نرى الميت ولا
نشاهد منكرا ونكيرا ولا نسمع صوتهما في السؤال ولا صوت الميت في الجواب،
فهذا يلزمه منه أن ينكر مشاهدة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لجبريل عليه
السلام وسماعه كلامه وسماع جبريل جوابه ولا يستطيع مصدق الشرع أن ينكر ذلك،
إذ ليس فيه إلا أن الله تعالى خلق له سماعا لذلك الصوت ومشاهدة لذلك الشخص،
ولم يخلق للحاضرين عنده ولا لعائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها وقد كانت تكون عنده
حاضرة في وقت ظهور بركات الوحي، فانكار هذا مصدره الإلحاد وإنكار سعة
القدرة، وقد فرغنا عن إبطاله ويلزم منه أيضا إنكار ما يشاهده النائم ويسمعه
من الأصوات الهائلة المزعجة، ولولا التجربة لبادر إلى الانكار كل من سمع من
النائم حكاية أحواله، فتعسا لمن ضاقت حوصلته عن تقدير اتساع القدرة لهذه
الأمور المستحقرة بالاضافة إلى خلق السموات والأرض وما بينهما، مع ما فيهما
من العجائب. والسبب الذي ينفر طباع  أهل الضلال عن التصديق بهذه الأمور
بعينه منفر عن التصديق بخلق الانسان من نطفة قذرة مع ما فيه من العجائب
والآيات أولا أن المشاهدة تضطره إلى التصديق فإذا ما لا برهان على إحالته
لا ينبغي أن ينكر بمجرد الاستبعاد. والإنسان لا يفهم بجميع بدنه بل بجزء من
باطن قلبه، واحياء جزء يفهم السؤال ويجيب ممكن مقدور عليه، فيبقى قول
القائل إنا نرى الميت ولا نشاهد منكرا ونكيرا ولا نسمع صوتهما في السؤال
ولا صوت الميت في الجواب، فهذا يلزمه منه أن ينكر مشاهدة النبي صلى الله
عليه وسلم لجبريل عليه السلام وسماعه كلامه وسماع جبريل جوابه ولا يستطيع
مصدق الشرع أن ينكر ذلك، إذ ليس فيه إلا أن الله تعالى خلق له سماعا لذلك
الصوت ومشاهدة لذلك الشخص، ولم يخلق للحاضرين عنده ولا لعائشة رضي الله
تعالى عنها وقد كانت تكون عنده حاضرة في وقت ظهور بركات الوحي، فانكار هذا
مصدره الإلحاد وإنكار سعة القدرة، وقد فرغنا عن إبطاله ويلزم منه أيضا
إنكار ما يشاهده النائم ويسمعه من الأصوات الهائلة المزعجة، ولولا التجربة
لبادر إلى الانكار كل من سمع من النائم حكاية أحواله، فتعسا لمن ضاقت
حوصلته عن تقدير اتساع القدرة لهذه الأمور المستحقرة بالاضافة إلى خلق
السموات والأرض وما بينهما، مع ما فيهما من العجائب. والسبب الذي ينفر طباع
أهل الضلال عن التصديق بهذه الأمور بعينه منفر عن التصديق بخلق الانسان من
نطفة قذرة مع ما فيه من العجائب والآيات أولا أن المشاهدة تضطره إلى
التصديق فإذا ما لا برهان على إحالته لا ينبغي أن ينكر بمجرد الاستبعاد.
وأما الميزان فهو أيضا حق وقد دلت عليه قواطع السمع، وهو ممكن فوجب
التصديق به. فإن قيل: كيف توزن الأعمال وهي أعراض وقد انعدمت، والمعدوم لا
يوزن؟ وإن قدرت إعادتها وخلقها في جسم الميزان كان محالا لاستحالة إعادة
الأعراض. ثم كيف تخلق حركة يد الانسان وهي طاعته في جسم الميزان؟ أيتحرك
بها الميزان فيكون ذلك حركة الميزان لا حركة يد الانسان  أم لا تتحرك فتكون
الحركة قد فاتت بجسم
ليس هو متحركا بها، وهو محال؟ ثم إن تحرك فيتفاوت من الميزان بقدر طول
الحركات وكثرتها لا بقدر مراتب الأجور، فرب حركة بجرء من البدن يزيد إثمها
على حركة جميع البدن فراسخ فهذا محال. فنقول: قد سئل النبي صلى الله عليه
وسلم عن هذا فقال: " توزن صحائف الأعمال فإن الكرام الكاتبين يكتبون
الأعمال في صحائف هي أجسام، فإذا وضعت في الميزان خلق الله تعالى في كفتها
ميلا بقدر رتبة الطاعات وهو على ما يشاء قدير ".
فإن قيل: فأي فائدة في هذا؟ وما معنى المحاسبة؟ قلنا: لا نطلب لفعل الله
تعالى فائدة: " لا يسأل عما يفعل وهو يسألون ". تم قد دللنا على هذا. ثم أي
بعد في أن تكون الفائدة فيه أن يشاهد العبد مقدار أعماله ويعلم أنه مجزي
بها بالعدل أو يتجاوز عنه باللطف، ومن يعزم على معاقبة وكيله بجنايته في
أمواله أو يعزم على الإبراء فمن أين يبعد أن يعرفه مقدار جنايته بأوضح
الطرق ليعلم أنه في عقوبته عادل وفي التجاوز عنه متفضل. هذا إن طلبت
الفائدة لأفعال الله تعالى، وقد سبق بطلان ذلك. وأما الصراط فهو أيضا حق،
والتصديق به واجب، لأنه ممكن. فإنه عبارة عن جسر ممدود على متن جهنم يرده
الخلق كافة، فإذا توافوا عليه قيل للملائكة " وقفوهم إنهم مسؤولون " فإن
قيل: كيف يمكن ذلك وفيما روى أدق من الشعر وأحد من السيف، فكيف يمكن المرور
عليه؟ قلنا هذا إن صدر ممن ينكر قدرة الله تعالى، فالكلام معه في إثبات
عموم قدرته وقد فرغنا عنها. وإن صدر من معترف بالقدرة فليس المشي على هذا
بأعجب من المشي في الهواء، والرب تعالى قادر على خلق قدرة عليه، ومعناه أن
يخلق له قدرة المشي على الهواء ولا يخلق في ذاته هويا إلى أسفل، ولا في
الهواء انحراف، فإذا أمكن هذا في الهواء فالصراط أثبت من الهواء بكل حال.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ش-ر (ḥ-sh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To gather, assemble, drive together (as cattle are herded); the Day of Gathering (Yawm al-Ḥashr).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The eschatological assembling of all created beings for judgment; a Quranic technical term for the general resurrection.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in reference to physical gathering; metaphorically extended to the re-creation of bodies.
- Root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To return, to restore, to repeat an act; the second occurrence of a thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Re-creation (iʿādat al-khalq) as a second origination (inshāʾ thānī), distinguished from the first only by temporal priority.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal when applied to the restoration of the identical body; metaphorical if only similars (amthāl) are restored.
- Root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Likeness, similitude, equivalent; a thing that corresponds to another in essence or attributes.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The distinction between the resurrected (al-muʿād) as the very same entity (ʿayn) versus its mere likeness (mithl); a crux in kalām discussions of personal identity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for exact identity; metaphorical for resemblance without numerical sameness.
- Root: م-ي-ز (m-y-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To separate, distinguish, discriminate between two things.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The epistemological criterion by which the resurrected is known to be the original, not a mere replica.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in the sense of discernment; used here to frame the logical problem of identity across non-existence.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Interrogative Constructions (al-Sharṭ wa-l-Istifhām) — The text employs "fa-in qīla" (if it is said) to introduce objections, followed by "qulnā" (we say) for the response; this dialogical structure requires careful tracking of the protasis and apodosis to preserve the argumentative flow.
chapters.translation:
I say: As for the Resurrection (al-ḥashr), what is meant by it is the re-creation (iʿādat al-khalq) of created beings, and the decisive scriptural proofs (al-qawāṭiʿ al-sharʿiyyah) have indicated it. It is possible, as demonstrated by the proof of the initial origination (al-ibtidāʾ). For re-creation is a second creation (khalq thānin), and there is no difference between it and the initial origination; it is only called "re-creation" by relation to the prior origination. And the One who is powerful over origination and initial creation is powerful over re-creation. This is the meaning of His saying: {«Say: He will give them life who produced them the first time»} (Q. 36:79).

If it is said: "Then what do you say — do the substances (jawāhir) and accidents (aʿrāḍ) become non-existent, and then both are re-created together? Or do the accidents become non-existent without the substances, and only the accidents are re-created?" — We say: All of that is possible, and there is no decisive scriptural proof specifying one of these possibilities. One of the two views is that the accidents become non-existent while the body of the human remains, having been transformed into the form of dust, for example; thus life, color, moisture, composition, shape, and a host of accidents have departed from it. The meaning of their re-creation is that those very accidents are restored to it, or their similars are restored to it. For according to us, the accident does not persist (lā yabqā), and life is an accident; what exists for us in every moment is another accident. The human is that same human by virtue of his body, for it is one, not by virtue of his accidents; for every accident that is renewed is other than the previous one. Thus it is not a condition of re-creation that one posit the re-creation of accidents. We have only mentioned this because some of our companions (al-aṣḥāb) held the impossibility of re-creating accidents — and that is false — but the discourse on refuting it would be lengthy, and there is no need for it in this our purpose.

The other view is that the bodies also become non-existent, and then the bodies are re-created by being invented a second time.

If it is said: "In what then does the resurrected (al-muʿād) differ from its mere likeness (al-mithl)? And what is the meaning of your saying that the resurrected is the very same as the first (ʿayn al-awwal), when no ʿayn (essence) of the non-existent remains to be re-created?" — We say: The non-existent is divided in God's knowledge into that which has previously had existence and that which has not previously had existence, just as non-existence in eternity (al-ʿadam fī al-azal) is divided into that which will have existence and that which God, exalted, knows will not exist. This division in God's knowledge cannot be denied. Knowledge encompasses all, and power is vast. So the meaning of re-creation is that we bestow existence upon that non-existence which has previously had existence; and the meaning of "likeness" is that existence is invented for a non-existence that has not previously had existence. This is the meaning of re-creation. And whenever the body is deemed to persist, and the matter is referred to the renewal of accidents that resemble the first ones, then the truth of the Law is affirmed, and one is delivered from the problem of re-creation and the distinction between the resurrected and the likeness.

We have spoken at length on this question in the book al-Tahāfut (The Incoherence), where we pursued the refutation of their doctrine by affirming the persistence of the soul (baqāʾ al-nafs), which according to them is non-spatial (ghayr mutaḥayyiz), and by positing the return of its governance (tadbīr) to the body — whether that body is the very body of the human or another. That, however, is an imposition (ilzām) that does not accord with what we ourselves believe; for that book was composed to refute their doctrine, not to establish the true doctrine. But since they deemed that the human is what he is by virtue of his soul, and that its occupation with governance is like an accident to it, and the body is a mere instrument for it, we imposed upon them — given their belief in the soul's persistence — the necessity of affirming re-creation, namely, by the soul's return to the governance of some body among bodies.

Now, the investigation into the verification of this chapter would lead to an inquiry into the spirit (al-rūḥ), the soul (al-nafs), life (al-ḥayāh), and their realities. But creedal matters (al-muʿtaqadāt) do not bear penetration to such depths in the intelligibles. What we have mentioned suffices for the exposition of moderation in belief (al-iqtiṣād fī al-iʿtiqād) regarding the affirmation of what the Law has brought.

As for the torment of the grave (ʿadhāb al-qabr), the decisive proofs of the Law have indicated it, since it was transmitted by multiple chains (tawātur) from the Prophet, peace be upon him, and from the Companions, may God be pleased with them, seeking refuge from it in their supplications. And his saying, peace be upon him, when passing by two graves, is well-known: "Verily, the two of them are being tormented." And His saying, exalted, has indicated it: {«And the evil torment encompassed the people of Pharaoh — the Fire, to which they are exposed morning and evening»} (Q. 40:45–46). It is possible, so affirmation of it is obligatory.

The manner of its possibility is evident. Only the Muʿtazila deny it, saying: "We see the person of the dead with our own eyes, and he is not being tormented; and the dead man may be torn apart by beasts and eaten." This is delusion (hawas). As for the observation of the person, it is observation of the outward aspects of the body; and the perceiver of punishment is a part of the heart or of the inner being, however that may be. It is not a necessary consequence of torment that motion appear in the outward body. Indeed, one who looks at the outward state of a sleeper does not observe what the sleeper perceives of pleasure during a wet dream, or of pain when imagining a beating or the like. And if the sleeper awoke and told of his visions, pains, and pleasures to one who had never had experience of sleep, that one would hasten to denial, deceived by the stillness of his body's outward state — just as the Muʿtazila's denial of the torment of the grave is an observation-based denial.

As for that which the beasts eat, the most that can be said is that the belly of the beast becomes a grave. The restoration of life to a part that perceives torment is possible; for not every sufferer perceives pain from his entire body.

As for the questioning of Munkar and Nakīr, it is true, and affirmation of it is obligatory, because the Law has brought it and it is possible. For it requires of them only an understanding conveyed by a voice or without a voice, and it requires of the one questioned only comprehension; and comprehension requires only life. The human does not comprehend with his entire body, but with a part of the interior of his heart. And the revivification of a part that comprehends the question and answers is possible and within divine power.

Thus there remains the saying of one who says: "We see the dead, and we do not observe Munkar and Nakīr, nor do we hear their voices in the questioning, nor the voice of the dead in the answering." This would oblige him to deny the Prophet's, peace be upon him, seeing of Gabriel, peace be upon him, and his hearing of his speech, and Gabriel's hearing of his reply. And no one who affirms the Law can deny that; for in it there is only that God, exalted, created for him a hearing for that voice and a sight for that person, and did not create it for those present with him, nor for ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, though she would be present with him at the time of the manifestation of the blessings of revelation. Denial of this stems from heresy (ilḥād) and denial of the vastness of divine power (saʿat al-qudrah), and we have already finished refuting that. It would also oblige one to deny what the sleeper sees and hears of terrifying, alarming voices. Were it not for experience, everyone who heard a sleeper narrate his states would hasten to denial. So woe to him whose capacity is too narrow to conceive the vastness of divine power for these matters that are contemptible in comparison to the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, along with the wonders they contain!

The very cause that repels the natures of the people of error from affirming these matters is the same cause that repels them from affirming the creation of the human from a filthy drop of fluid, despite what it contains of wonders and signs. First, because direct observation compels one to affirm [the latter]; so whatever has no proof of its impossibility ought not to be denied merely on the basis of improbability (istibʿād).

As for the Balance (al-mīzān), it too is true, and the decisive proofs of revelation have indicated it, and it is possible, so affirmation of it is obligatory.

If it is said: "How are deeds weighed, when they are accidents that have become non-existent, and the non-existent cannot be weighed? And if you suppose their re-creation and their creation in the body of the Balance, that would be impossible, given the impossibility of re-creating accidents. Then how is the movement of a human's hand — which is his act of obedience — created in the body of the Balance? Does the Balance move with it, so that it becomes the movement of the Balance, not the movement of the human's hand? Or does it not move, so that the movement would have perished in a body that is not moving with it — which is impossible? And even if it moves, the Balance would tip according to the length and multiplicity of movements, not according to the ranks of rewards; for a movement of a part of the body may have a sin greater than a movement of the entire body over leagues — this is impossible." — We say: The Prophet, peace be upon him, was asked about this, and he said: "The scrolls of deeds are weighed; for the noble scribes write the deeds on scrolls that are bodies. When they are placed in the Balance, God, exalted, creates in its pan an inclination (mayl) proportionate to the rank of the acts of obedience — and He is powerful over whatever He wills."

If it is said: "Then what benefit is there in this? And what is the meaning of the reckoning (al-muḥāsabah)?" — We say: We do not seek a benefit for God's act, exalted: {«He is not asked about what He does, but they will be asked»} (Q. 21:23). We have already demonstrated this. Then, what remoteness is there in that the benefit is that the servant witnesses the measure of his deeds and knows that he is recompensed for them with justice, or that he is pardoned with grace (luṭf)? For one who resolves to punish his agent for his offense regarding his wealth, or resolves to absolve him — how far is it that he should make known to him the measure of his offense by the clearest means, so that he knows that in punishing he is just, and in pardoning he is gracious? This is if you seek a benefit for God's acts — and the falsity of that has already preceded.

As for the Path (al-ṣirāṭ), it too is true, and affirmation of it is obligatory, because it is possible. For it is a bridge stretched over the surface of Hell, which all creatures will pass. When they gather upon it, it is said to the angels: {«Stop them; indeed, they are to be questioned»} (Q. 37:24).

If it is said: "How is that possible, given what has been narrated — that it is finer than a hair and sharper than a sword? How can passage upon it be possible?" — We say: If this comes from one who denies the power of God, exalted, then the discourse with him concerns establishing the universality of His power, and we have already finished that. If it comes from one who acknowledges the power, then walking upon this is no more wondrous than walking in the air. The Lord, exalted, is powerful over creating a power for it: that is, He creates for him the power to walk upon the air, and does not create in his essence a downward fall, nor in the air any deviation. If this is possible in the air, then the Path is more stable than the air in every respect.

chapters.title_en: Section 34 — Apology for Omitting Chapters with Which the Creeds Were Charged
chapters.arabic_text:
### | الفصل الثاني:

### | في الاعتذار عن الإخلال بفصول

### | شحنت بها المعتقدات فرأيت الإعراض  عن ذكرها أولى لأن المعتقدات المختصرة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ذ-ر (ʿ-dh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes "excuse" or "apology" — the act of clearing oneself from blame or deficiency, with a nuance of covering a fault (ʿudhr) as a shield.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, ʿudhr signifies a legitimate ground for remission of obligation, often tied to divine grace (faḍl) or human incapacity (ʿajz), not moral failure.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — an explicit plea of justification; metaphorical (majāz) — the omission itself becomes an implicit apology, as here the author's silence is the excuse.
- Root: ش-ح-ن (sh-ḥ-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning "to fill, load, or charge" — often used for filling a vessel or charging a container to capacity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Metaphysically, sh-ḥ-n implies saturating a text with content, but here it carries a pejorative nuance — overloading creeds with excessive detail that may distract from essential belief.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical filling; metaphorical — intellectual or doctrinal saturation, where the author deems the load excessive and thus chooses omission.
- Root: أ-ع-ر-ض (a-ʿ-r-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To turn away, avert, or disregard" — from ʿarḍ (side), implying turning one's face or attention aside.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, iʿrāḍ denotes deliberate neglect of a topic, often for strategic or pedagogical reasons — not ignorance but chosen restraint.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical turning away; metaphorical — intellectual dismissal, here framed as a virtue (awlā) rather than a defect.
- Sībawayh Rule: **Al-Istithnāʾ al-Munqaṭiʿ** (Discontinuous Exception) — The phrase "رأيت الإعراض عن ذكرها أولى" (I saw that turning away from mentioning them is more fitting) employs a comparative (afʿal al-tafḍīl) that implicitly excludes the omitted chapters from the category of necessary content, requiring the reader to infer the unstated contrast (i.e., omission is better than inclusion for brevity's sake).
